info.title: Agent hub /v1 contract — single source of truth for hub<->consumer surface
info.description:
GENERATED from contract/v1.json and contract/errors.json by scripts/emit-openapi.mjs — do not edit this file; edit the contract and regenerate.

This document covers the HTTP surface only. The adapter protocol (the hub talking to a harness plugin over stdio JSON-RPC) is NOT HTTP and lives in contract/adapter-v1.json, which is machine-checked against every manifest, every request the hub sends, every event an adapter emits and every event the hub handles.

The running hub reports the exact contract it was built against at GET /v1/hub/surface (`contract.sha256`), so a client can prove which document it is talking to.

Paths, request shapes, response shapes, SSE event objects and error codes live here, and this file is checked, not merely written down: the hub reports its own surface at GET /v1/hub/surface and the hub refuses to START when the two disagree in either direction (boot self-check, server.mjs). So change this file when you change the surface — the check is what makes that instruction true instead of a hope. Adapter-facing surface lives in adapter-v1.json.

servers.description: the hub binds a loopback port chosen at start; the port and the bearer token are in <DATA_DIR>/endpoint.json

get.description: the harnesses this hub has registered: a plugin that is present is registered on first sight, with its declared capabilities and status. `GET /v1/hub/harnesses` is the management view of the same registry (installed extensions, runtime, timestamps). This is the ONE route that answers without a token: discovery is open, everything else is 401 unauthorized.

next_cursor.description: reserved seat: no cursor is implemented, this is always null

note.description: present only when the list is EMPTY: where the hub searched for plugins, and the two ways to give it one. An empty catalogue with no reason is indistinguishable from a broken hub

get.description: the models THIS HARNESS CAN RUN — the single authoritative source for model selection, and the only list a caller needs (do not merge it with API 1). One query: the harness's own catalog plus every core-managed provider the harness can reach during a session, so an entry means the same thing whichever harness answered and whichever way a provider got there (native config, like dsh, or injected at session start, like pi). An injected provider is named `hub-<coreProviderId>` in every harness — one spelling, no slash (pi splits a model reference on the first slash) — and `modelProviderId` accepts that spelling or the bare `<coreProviderId>`. capability-gated; known:false = harness declares no models capability (never faked as empty). Each entry keeps its real providerId. `thinkingLevels` is the list the model's configuration states, passed through verbatim: null = nothing was stated, [] = an empty list was stated, a list = exactly those names in that order. The core derives nothing from it (no vocabulary, no source label, no per-model verdict) and neither does a caller have to. A model id is unique only with its providerId; (providerId, id) is the key.

get.description: the hub's harness registry. The hub manages harnesses, not just lists them: for each one it holds whether it is enabled and which extensions and skills are installed for it. A plugin present under the plugins directory is registered on first sight, carrying the extensions its manifest declares; a plugin that is gone keeps its row marked missing. Each harness row's `availableExtensions` is the catalogue THAT plugin ships (its own `extensions/` directories, and the only extensions that harness may be given); the top-level `availableExtensions` is the union of ids across installed plugins. Extensions are installed BY the hub: before a harness runs, the hub writes that harness's selected extension directories into its data dir, and the adapter places them where its harness reads them.

post.description: A `title` is pushed to the harness when the session starts (capability `rename`); without that capability the title stays in the hub and the answer says so in `warning`. Every session runs its harness in the hub's OWN data dir; there is no config-scope knob. The `system` scope was removed: it pointed the harness home at the user's real config (`~/.dsh`), attached to a dsh daemon the user happened to be running, and — worst — let the USER'S OWN settings decide the permission policy, so a session could run with approvals suppressed while the hub believed it was answering them. The user's configuration is still read once where a harness needs it (pi: its agent dir; dsh: `settings.yaml` minus the permission section), and nothing is written back.

patch.description: Change session configuration. modelProviderId selects another core-managed provider in the same conversation; credentials/grant precedes config/set. Supply modelId or retain the currently selected model. Provider switching requires an idle turn and is serialized against turn admission and lifecycle mutations. Session id and native ref are preserved. Missing credentials/unknown provider fail before injection. Failed application retains saved selection and drops the changed adapter so next use restores saved configuration. Applied provider/model must be confirmed by the adapter. thinkingLevel sets the harness-native thinking level for this session; unconfirmed application is reported as null plus a warning, never as the requested value. A level the model does not offer is 400 validation_failed. `title` renames the session in the HARNESS as well (the hub is not the only place a name is shown): the adapter answers with the title the harness accepted, which may differ from the one asked for (dsh normalizes and sanitises), and the session reports both — `title` what was asked, `appliedTitle` what the harness holds. Requires the harness capability `rename` (501 unsupported otherwise). A title the harness did not accept is an error, never a hub-only rename that looks applied. Refused with 409 session_busy while a turn is running, like every other PATCH knob. Policy-only PATCH containing plan/review may apply during a running or waiting turn when the adapter is ready. Cancellation and model/provider/thinking/preset changes still require idle. Review changes affect future tool calls; already pending approvals/questions remain explicit decisions, never auto-approved. Applied fields must confirm actual state. modelProviderId also accepts an available native provider/model pair from this harness catalogue; native credentials remain harness-private and no hub credential is granted. Model switches return the observed thinking level for the selected model.

get.description: The skills THIS session's harness actually has, read from the harness itself (pi/jouzu: their own command list; dsh: its skill catalogue RPC) — not a list of what the hub installed. It is per SESSION, not per harness, because a catalogue depends on the session's own directory: dsh resolves the project root from the session header, and the pi family also reads the project's `.pi/skills`. The difference between installed and seen is the point: the hub writes a skill's bytes into the harness's own skills directory before its process starts, and a harness may still refuse one silently (dsh drops a skill whose name is not kebab-case, whose description is missing, whose invocation keys are camelCase, or that is not a single-level `<id>/SKILL.md` bundle). Requires the harness capability `skills` (501 unsupported otherwise). A harness that does not answer in time is reported as `known:false` with a `reason` — never as an empty catalogue: an empty list is a claim ('it has no skills') and a timeout is not evidence for it. (jouzu finishes its own startup lazily: its first answer measured 9s once and 70s once, its second 24ms.)

known.description: false when this harness cannot report a catalogue at all

reason.description: why the catalogue is unknown (present only when known is false)

post.description: register a provider: `{id?, label?, url, api?, token?, scope?, declarations?}`. The id is generated when absent; a duplicate id is refused (409). `api` is the wire protocol the provider speaks in the harness vocabulary (openai-completions, anthropic-messages, openai-responses, ...); the adapter that writes the harness's own provider entry is what validates it. `declarations` is keyed by model id — what that model accepts (thinking levels, window, limits) — because a provider's model list does not carry any of it. A declaration may also carry `input` — the modalities the model takes ("text", "image") — because a model that does not state them is not advertised as taking images. A declaration may also carry `name` (the display name; the harness shows it instead of the id) and `cost` ({input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite} per million tokens, optional tiers). Optional immutable providerType/providerTypeVersion select an installed type. Omitted values select custom-compatible v1 for compatibility. Explicit unknown type/version is rejected before storing credentials. Endpoint requirements and configuration validation belong to the selected type: a type that accepts a caller endpoint requires url; a type that owns its endpoint supplies it and rejects overrides. Fields are the configuration.fields its descriptor declares.

post.description: Ask the harness to compact the session's own conversation. The hub does not compact anything itself and does not compute the numbers: it reports what the harness says (source:'harness'). Fields a harness does not report are ABSENT, never zero — pi counts the replaced span and then estimates the rebuilt context, dsh counts the replaced span only. A harness with nothing worth compacting answers compacted:false with its own words in `detail`; a compaction that failed answers compact_failed. Refused (409 session_busy) while a turn is running, because pi's compact aborts the running turn and a hub must not throw away work to run a maintenance call. Requires the harness capability `compact` (501 unsupported otherwise). The same facts also arrive on the turn stream as `session.compacting` then `session.compacted` — including for a compaction the harness performed on its own (a full context compacts mid-turn), which nobody asked for.

post.description: install a plugin. Two sources, one landing rule: what lands is a directory with a manifest, under the id that manifest declares, in the hub's OWN plugins root (<DATA_DIR>/plugins). `{source:{url, ref?}}` clones a git repository (a URL or a local path); `{source:{artifact:{url, sha256, id, version, size?}}}` downloads a release zip and verifies it — size first, then sha256 — before anything is unpacked. An id the hub already installed is REPLACED: that is what updating is, and it is the same primitive because the only difference is whether a directory was already there. The old copy is moved aside first and removed only after the new one is in place, so a failure at any step leaves the previous plugin exactly as it was. An id living in a directory this hub does not own (AGENT_HUB_PLUGINS_DIR, a deployment's checkout) is refused with 409: that tree is somebody else's. A harness with open sessions is refused (409 `plugin_in_use`, naming them) rather than replaced under a running process. The response says `updated`, and the plugin's runtime is prepared by the adapter in the background.

updated.description: true when an id the hub had installed was replaced

A model named without a provider must belong to the provider that is in effect — a model from elsewhere is refused (400 validation_failed), never accepted and left to fail mid-turn.

appliedModel.description: the model the adapter actually applied; compared against modelId (T0: a silent fallback fails loudly)

appliedProviderId.description: the provider route the adapter actually applied (hub/<id> for an injected hub provider); proof the requested provider was used, not the harness's own

plan.description: the plan mode this session asked for; null = do not intervene, the harness keeps its own state

appliedPlan.description: the plan state the adapter actually applied (proof, like appliedModel); null = no plan capability, or not yet known

review.description: ask before every tool call (the review switch); null = do not intervene

appliedReview.description: the review state the adapter actually applied (proof, like appliedModel); null = no review capability, or not yet known

cwd.description: Resolved working directory, passed to adapters as AGENT_HUB_CWD. On creation, omitted/null/empty cwd allocates a persistent core-managed directory under the existing data root. This is a working-directory boundary, not OS-level confinement.

turnRunning.description: The hub's own verdict that this session has a turn admitted and not yet finished (admitted/running/awaiting_approval/awaiting_question/cancelling). Published so a client renders this fact instead of re-deriving it from activeTurn.state with its own copy of the state list - a second authority that drifts from this one.

additionalDirectories.description: extra roots the harness may activate, in addition to cwd; absolute paths. Passed through to the harness — whether a harness supports them is the harness's business, and the core neither refuses nor silently drops them. [] or null = none.

appliedAdditionalDirectories.description: what the harness reported about additionalDirectories: {requested, applied, supported, reason}. The core passes the roots through and records the harness's own answer; it never assumes they became active.

disabledTools.description: the tool names the caller asked to disable; null = never asked

appliedTools.description: the disabled set the harness reported it actually has; null = not observed. A switch that could not be confirmed must not read as success.

deleted.description: true once the session has been deleted from session/list (ACP session/delete). The record is kept; delete removes it from the list, it does not wipe it.

source.description: Origin of the message, separate from model-facing role. Harness-generated continuations are not human input.

reasoning.description: Reasoning text returned by the native session, when present; never reconstructed from assistant prose.

nativeId.description: Native persisted entry identity if distinct from the stable adapter message id.

tools.description: Native tool calls belonging to this message, correlated to results by toolCallId, not positional inference.

contentPart.description: one part of a turn's content. text is plain. image carries base64 bytes — the media type is the harness-facing one (image/png, image/jpeg, image/webp, image/gif), data is raw base64 with NO data: prefix.

data.description: type=image: base64 bytes, no data: prefix

tool.description: confirm | select — the kind of dialog the harness raised

options.description: for a select dialog: the choices the harness offered (e.g. Allow Once / Allow Always / Reject); decision echoes one of these

reason.description: user-supplied rejection reason when the harness asked for one (codex denied.rejection; pi/jouzu Reject with Reason). null when the harness has no such concept (dsh) or the user gave none

question.description: A harness asking the user to decide something. Distinct from `approval`: an approval permits one action (allow/deny); a question asks for an answer, possibly with several options and supporting detail, and the answer is data the harness reads back

detail.description: supporting text rendered with the question (e.g. the plan under review); never an option label

intent.description: presentation hint: what kind of decision this is. `{ kind: 'plan-review', approve: '<label>' }` says detail is a plan and names the approving label. Presentation only — the answer carries the same fields either way

answers.description: the user's answer, once given: one entry per asked question

preset.description: A preset as the CLIENT sees it: an opaque id plus metadata. Content is NOT carried cross-wire (dsh-aligned; reading a composition is reconnaissance). The harness/adapter owns what a preset id means; core does not interpret it.

id.description: opaque preset id; the only thing needed to select it

name.description: display name published by the harness; falls back to id

trust.description: shipped with the deployment or locally authored (dsh: a user preset is exactly as privileged as the plugins it names)

isDefault.description: whether a session that names no preset gets this one

broken.description: why this preset cannot compose a session; absent when it can

enabled.description: false = disabled; honest grading — adapter must not report a tool disabled unless it actually blocks it

artifact.description: one release artifact: the zip, and the digest that makes it verifiable

url.description: http(s) URL of the release zip

sha256.description: 64 hex characters; the artifact is refused unless the download hashes to exactly this

id.description: the plugin id the archive must declare in its manifest

version.description: which release this artifact is (the harness version its manifest pins)

size.description: the artifact's byte size; checked as well, so a truncated download is caught even when it happens to hash the same (it cannot, but the size is also what makes a 0-byte or half-written file obvious)

retryable.description: whether retrying the same request unchanged can succeed — straight from contract/errors.json, the same table that decides the status, so body, status and table cannot disagree. false means something must change first (the session is busy, the state needs repair, the input is invalid).

whether retrying the same request unchanged can succeed. It comes from contract/errors.json — the same table that decides the status — so the body, the status and the table cannot disagree. false means something must change first (the session is busy, the state needs repair, the input is invalid).

modelInvocable.description: whether the MODEL may load it; false means a human must invoke it

origin.description: 'deployment' when it came from the plugins directory this hub was given, 'hub' when the hub installed it into its own root

source.description: the git URL this hub installed it from; null when nobody installed it (a checkout or a deployment's directory)

runtime.description: {package, version, target} as the manifest declares it; null when the plugin brings its own runtime

runtimeReady.description: whether the declared runtime command exists on disk — a filesystem fact, not a claim that the harness works

prepare.description: {state: running|ready|failed, detail, startedAt, finishedAt} of the last runtime/prepare for this plugin, or null when none ran in this process

invalid.description: why the manifest cannot be honoured; null when it can

artifact.description: {id, version, url, sha256, size} exactly as the install named it, when this plugin came from a release artifact; null for a git source or a directory nobody installed. A client compares `version` with a catalog entry to know an update exists — the hub does not compare anything itself.

catalogVersion.description: one release of a plugin, as the registry file states it (stored verbatim, never resolved or rewritten by the hub)

catalogEntry.description: one plugin the registry file lists; extra fields are kept as the author wrote them

kind.description: 'harness' or 'provider' — what the plugin is, as the registry declares it

name.description: display name; the client localises what it can and shows this otherwise

versions.description: newest first: the entry a client installs or updates to is versions[0]

event_turn_admitted.description: the turn is accepted and the stream is open

event_message_delta.description: one delta of the streaming answer; kind says whether it is text or the model thinking out loud

args.description: Structured invocation arguments when supplied by the adapter.

result.description: Original structured tool result when supplied by the adapter; detail remains a short summary.

event_question_requested.description: question is not approval: this wants an ANSWER, not permission

event_plan_changed.description: plan mode changed — possibly because the HARNESS changed it (a model leaving plan when its plan is approved), which is why the hub reports it instead of assuming its own last request held

event_session_stats.description: plus whatever the harness reports about this session: tokens?, cost?, context?, turns?, messages? — a field it does not report is absent

event_session_compacting.description: the harness is rewriting its own context right now, whether or not this session asked for it

event_session_compacted.description: the same facts the compact route answers with, for a compaction the harness performed on its own

event_session_renamed.description: the HARNESS named or renamed the session (dsh titles a session from its first prompt); the hub follows instead of keeping a title only it believes in

event_session_notification.description: Harness notification, not model output. Live stream only; no durable notification history promised.

event_hub_plugins_changed.description: the set of installed plugins changed (installed | removed | runtime | subscribed); re-read what you show
